proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Purpose
proposals.statement: Enterprise Architecture defines the guardrails that must be respected.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Purpose
proposals.statement: Each product may have its own roadmap, backlog and release cycle, but the solution must still behave as one coherent operational capability.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Purpose
proposals.statement: Solution Architecture is required when products must share interfaces, exchange data, align security assumptions, operate in a common runtime or deployment topology, verify integrated behavior, or remain compatible with a solution release baseline.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Purpose
proposals.statement: The purpose of this document is therefore to define the minimum solution-level architecture guidance required for product participation, capability allocation, cross-product interfaces, data flows, security boundaries, deployment assumptions, integration evidence, release compatibility, solution runway, technical debt and solution quality markers.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Level Architecture / Solution Level Architecture Scope
proposals.statement: Solution Architecture governs the architecture concerns that arise when multiple products must work together as one coherent and releasable solution.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Level Architecture / Solution Level Architecture Scope
proposals.statement: Instead, it defines the cross-product structure required for integration, interoperability, security, data consistency, deployment alignment and release compatibility.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Level Architecture / Solution Architecture Decision Rights
proposals.statement: Cross-product interfaces | Which interfaces are required between products?

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Level Architecture / Solution Architecture Decision Rights
proposals.statement: Solution quality | Which quality scenarios must be verified at solution level?

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Level Architecture / Solution Architecture Decision Rights
proposals.statement: Architecture runway | Which technical enablers are required before release?

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Level Architecture / Solution Level Architecture Deliverables
proposals.statement: The following deliverables define the minimum set of solution-level architecture assets required to make multiple products work together as one coherent, integrated and releasable solution.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Level Architecture / Solution Level Architecture Deliverables
proposals.statement: Each solution deliverable should be owned, versioned and aligned with the applicable enterprise guardrails.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Level Architecture / Solution Level Architecture Deliverables
proposals.statement: Product Architects must be able to understand which solution decisions affect their products, which interfaces and data contracts must be implemented, which evidence is required, and how product releases are assessed for compatibility with the solution baseline.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Level Architecture / Solution Level Architecture Deliverables
proposals.statement: Where a deliverable is incomplete or unstable, the gap should be made visible as solution architecture runway, integration risk or solution-level technical debt.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Level Architecture / Solution Level Architecture Deliverables
proposals.statement: Integration and Verification Matrix | What must be proven, where, when, and by whom

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Level Architecture / Solution Level Architecture Deliverables
proposals.statement: Solution Process Model | Defines integration, verification, solution demo, and release mechanisms required by the solution architecture

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / BAPO Structure of the Solution Architecture
proposals.statement: The solution BAPO view should remain focused on architecture.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / BAPO Structure of the Solution Architecture
proposals.statement: It identifies only the process and ownership mechanisms required to keep the solution architecture aligned.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / BAPO Structure of the Solution Architecture
proposals.statement: For example, if the solution architecture depends on a stable cross-product interface, then the required process is interface review and contract testing, and the required ownership is an interface owner.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / BAPO Structure of the Solution Architecture
proposals.statement: If the solution architecture depends on a shared data model, then the required process is data contract validation, and the required ownership is a data owner.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / BAPO Structure of the Solution Architecture
proposals.statement: Process requirement | Integration cadence, contract testing, solution demo, verification, release approval, compatibility checks

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / BAPO Structure of the Solution Architecture
proposals.statement: Ownership requirement | Solution architect, product architects, interface owners, data owners, security owners, system team

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / BAPO Structure of the Solution Architecture
proposals.statement: Business needs such as customer value, mission effectiveness, interoperability and release agility must be reflected in solution architecture decisions for product participation, capability allocation, cross-product interfaces, data flows, security boundaries, deployment topology and solution baselines.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / BAPO Structure of the Solution Architecture
proposals.statement: These architecture decisions must define the minimum integration, verification and release processes required to keep the products compatible, including contract testing, solution demos, compatibility checks and release planning.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / BAPO Structure of the Solution Architecture
proposals.statement: Clear ownership is required across the Solution Architect, Product Architects, interface owners, data owners, security owners and system team so that the solution remains integrated, verifiable and releasable while individual products can continue to evolve.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Capability and Mission Thread Definition
proposals.statement: A solution architecture should define enough mission threads to prove the critical behavior of the solution.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Capability and Mission Thread Definition
proposals.statement: These mission threads should later become integration test scenarios and system demo scenarios.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Capability and Mission Thread Definition
proposals.statement: Business driver | The solution must deliver an end-to-end mission or business capability

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Capability and Mission Thread Definition
proposals.statement: Process requirement | Mission threads shall be used for integration tests and solution demos

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Capability and Mission Thread Definition
proposals.statement: Ownership requirement | Solution Architect owns capability architecture; Product Management owns capability priority

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Product Participation and Capability Allocation
proposals.statement: Product participation and capability allocation define which products contribute to a solution and which solution capabilities each product is responsible for.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Product Participation and Capability Allocation
proposals.statement: Solution Architecture must show how the required business or mission capability is decomposed into product contributions and how these contributions are integrated into one coherent solution baseline.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Product Participation and Capability Allocation
proposals.statement: Business driver | Multiple products must contribute coherently to one solution capability or mission outcome. | Ensures that product participation is driven by solution value, not by organizational convenience or historical product boundaries.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Product Participation and Capability Allocation
proposals.statement: Process requirement | Product participation and capability allocation must be reviewed during solution planning, PI planning, integration planning and release planning.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Product Participation and Capability Allocation
proposals.statement: Changes must be reflected in the solution baseline. | Ensures that capability allocation is not a static diagram, but remains aligned with planning, integration, verification and release decisions.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Product Participation and Capability Allocation
proposals.statement: Ownership requirement | The Solution Architect owns the overall capability allocation and product participation map.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Product Participation and Capability Allocation
proposals.statement: The product participation map should identify all products that contribute to the solution, the capabilities they provide, the interfaces they expose or consume, and the dependencies that affect integration and release compatibility.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Product Participation and Capability Allocation
proposals.statement: The capability-to-product matrix should make clear whether a capability is owned by one product, shared across several products, or still unresolved.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Product Participation and Capability Allocation
proposals.statement: Capability allocation should also identify architecture risks.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Product Participation and Capability Allocation
proposals.statement: A capability may be at risk if ownership is unclear, if several products provide overlapping functionality, if a required interface is not yet specified, if data ownership is missing, or if a product release is not compatible with the intended solution baseline.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Product Participation and Capability Allocation
proposals.statement: These risks should be captured as solution architecture runway, integration risks or solution-level technical debt.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Product Participation and Capability Allocation
proposals.statement: Where several products could provide the same capability, the Solution Architect should document the allocation rationale.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Product Participation and Capability Allocation
proposals.statement: This should include the reason for the selected product, rejected alternatives where relevant, expected integration impact, required interface or data contracts, and consequences for future product autonomy.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Product Participation and Capability Allocation
proposals.statement: Product participation and capability allocation must be updated whenever the solution scope, product contribution, interface ownership, release baseline or capability priority changes.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Product Participation and Capability Allocation
proposals.statement: A solution release baseline should not be considered complete unless the participating products and their allocated capabilities are clear, owned, evidenced and compatible.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Cross-Product Interface Architecture
proposals.statement: Cross-product interfaces must be treated as first-class architecture elements.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Cross-Product Interface Architecture
proposals.statement: They should not be left to individual teams to negotiate informally.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Cross-Product Interface Architecture
proposals.statement: Every cross-product interface should have an owner, version, contract, test strategy, compatibility rule, and deprecation rule.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Cross-Product Interface Architecture
proposals.statement: Business driver | Products must integrate reliably and release independently without breaking the solution

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Cross-Product Interface Architecture
proposals.statement: Process requirement | Contract testing, interface review, compatibility testing, and schema validation are required

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Cross-Product Interface Architecture
proposals.statement: Ownership requirement | Interface owners are mandatory for all cross-product interfaces

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Cross-Product Interface Architecture
proposals.statement: Cross-product interfaces should be managed as solution-level architecture artifacts.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Cross-Product Interface Architecture
proposals.statement: They should be visible in the solution interface catalogue and linked to the Product Architecture Documents of the providing and consuming products.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Cross-Product Interface Architecture
proposals.statement: Interface contracts should define not only technical structure, but also ownership, versioning, compatibility rules, security assumptions, error behavior and verification evidence.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Cross-Product Interface Architecture
proposals.statement: A cross-product interface should not be considered mature if it is negotiated informally, unowned, unversioned, untested or disconnected from the solution release baseline.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Cross-Product Interface Architecture
proposals.statement: Missing interface ownership, missing contract tests or unclear compatibility rules should be captured as solution technical debt, architecture runway or a release-readiness risk.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Data Flow and Semantic Alignment
proposals.statement: Solution data flow architecture should show how data moves from source to consumer across products.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Data Flow and Semantic Alignment
proposals.statement: It should also show where data is transformed, enriched, filtered, stored, classified, or exposed as a service.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Data Flow and Semantic Alignment
proposals.statement: Business driver | The solution must turn product-level data into mission-relevant information

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Data Flow and Semantic Alignment
proposals.statement: Process requirement | Data contracts require validation, review, and integration test evidence

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Data Flow and Semantic Alignment
proposals.statement: Ownership requirement | Data Architect and solution data owners are required

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Data Flow and Semantic Alignment
proposals.statement: The solution data flow model should identify the source, transformation, enrichment, storage, classification and consumption of data across participating products.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Data Flow and Semantic Alignment
proposals.statement: It should also show which product or role owns the meaning, quality and lifecycle of the data.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Data Flow and Semantic Alignment
proposals.statement: Semantic alignment must be reviewable through data contracts, schemas, topic definitions, metadata rules, classification rules and ownership records.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Data Flow and Semantic Alignment
proposals.statement: A solution should not be considered data-aligned if products exchange technically valid messages but interpret the meaning, units, timestamps, confidence values, classifications or lifecycle assumptions differently.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Data Flow and Semantic Alignment
proposals.statement: Where semantic alignment is incomplete, the gap should be captured as solution data debt, product follow-up action, data architecture runway or release-readiness risk.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Security and Trust Boundary Architecture
proposals.statement: This is required because security cannot be assessed only at the product level when identities, data flows, interfaces, deployment zones, operational roles and audit responsibilities span several products.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Security and Trust Boundary Architecture
proposals.statement: Solution Architecture must show where trust zones begin and end, which identities and access rules apply, where data crosses security boundaries, which cryptographic protections are required, how logging and audit evidence are collected, and how security assumptions remain compatible across the participating products.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Security and Trust Boundary Architecture
proposals.statement: Business driver | Cross-product operation requires consistent trust, protection, auditability and compliance across the complete solution. | Ensures that security is treated as a solution-level architecture concern, not only as separate product implementation detail.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Security and Trust Boundary Architecture
proposals.statement: Process requirement | Solution-level threat modelling, security architecture review, security verification and release-readiness checks are required. | Ensures that security assumptions are reviewed, verified and evidenced before the solution is released.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Security and Trust Boundary Architecture
proposals.statement: Ownership requirement | The Security Architect owns the solution security concept and trust-boundary model.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Security and Trust Boundary Architecture
proposals.statement: Evidence | Solution threat model, trust-zone diagram, identity and access model, crypto assumptions, security requirements, security test evidence, vulnerability findings, audit/logging evidence and product security declarations. | Makes solution security reviewable, testable and traceable across products.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Security and Trust Boundary Architecture
proposals.statement: The trust-boundary model should identify all relevant security zones, participating products, external systems, communication paths, identity providers, authorization points, crypto boundaries, logging responsibilities and audit-relevant events.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Security and Trust Boundary Architecture
proposals.statement: It should also show where data crosses boundaries between products, domains, classifications, runtime environments or operational responsibilities.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Security and Trust Boundary Architecture
proposals.statement: Solution-level security review should verify that the participating products share compatible security assumptions.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Security and Trust Boundary Architecture
proposals.statement: Security evidence must therefore be collected at both levels.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Security and Trust Boundary Architecture
proposals.statement: Product teams provide evidence that their product implements the required controls.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Security and Trust Boundary Architecture
proposals.statement: Gaps should be captured as solution security risks, product follow-up actions, architecture runway, technical debt or release-readiness blockers.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Security and Trust Boundary Architecture
proposals.statement: Where a product or solution cannot fully satisfy the solution security and trust-boundary expectations, the deviation shall be handled through the architecture exception process.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Security and Trust Boundary Architecture
proposals.statement: The exception must identify the affected security boundary, the risk, the owner, the mitigation, the review date and the impact on release readiness.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integrated Runtime and Deployment Architecture
proposals.statement: This is required because a solution may be architecturally correct on paper, but still fail in practice if runtime dependencies, deployment topology, infrastructure assumptions, configuration rules or environment constraints are not aligned.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integrated Runtime and Deployment Architecture
proposals.statement: Solution Architecture must show where solution components run, how products are distributed across edge, fog and cloud environments, which runtime dependencies exist, how configuration is managed, how services discover and communicate with each other, how observability is provided, and how deployment compatibility is verified before release.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integrated Runtime and Deployment Architecture
proposals.statement: Business driver | The solution must be deployable and operable in realistic mission, customer and operational environments. | Ensures that deployment architecture is driven by real operational constraints, not only by development or laboratory assumptions.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integrated Runtime and Deployment Architecture
proposals.statement: Process requirement | Deployment verification, environment compatibility checks, configuration validation and release-baseline alignment are required. | Ensures that deployment readiness is verified before the solution is declared release-compatible.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integrated Runtime and Deployment Architecture
proposals.statement: Ownership requirement | The Solution Architect owns the integrated deployment architecture.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integrated Runtime and Deployment Architecture
proposals.statement: The integrated deployment view should show all relevant runtime nodes, containers, services, products, infrastructure dependencies, network zones, communication paths and operational environments.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integrated Runtime and Deployment Architecture
proposals.statement: It should also identify which parts of the solution are deployed at the tactical edge, in fog-level mission infrastructure, in cloud environments or in hybrid configurations.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integrated Runtime and Deployment Architecture
proposals.statement: Deployment architecture must also make assumptions explicit.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integrated Runtime and Deployment Architecture
proposals.statement: This includes resource constraints, latency expectations, connectivity limitations, security zones, configuration dependencies, data locality, update windows, observability requirements and degraded-connectivity behavior.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integrated Runtime and Deployment Architecture
proposals.statement: Solution-level deployment verification should confirm that the participating products can be deployed together, configured consistently, monitored effectively and operated within the intended environment constraints.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integrated Runtime and Deployment Architecture
proposals.statement: Where runtime or deployment gaps are identified, they should be captured as solution architecture runway, deployment risk, product follow-up action, platform improvement or solution-level technical debt.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integrated Runtime and Deployment Architecture
proposals.statement: A solution release baseline should not be considered complete unless the deployment topology, runtime dependencies, configuration assumptions and environment compatibility are sufficiently defined, owned and evidenced.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integrated Runtime and Deployment Architecture
proposals.statement: Product Release | A release of a single product that must remain compatible with one or more solution baselines

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integrated Runtime and Deployment Architecture
proposals.statement: BAPO element | Required content for a solution release baseline

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integrated Runtime and Deployment Architecture
proposals.statement: The solution baseline should be maintained as a living artifact.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integrated Runtime and Deployment Architecture
proposals.statement: Product teams should know which solution baselines they support.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integrated Runtime and Deployment Architecture
proposals.statement: Solution release decisions should be based on verified compatibility, not on assumed compatibility.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Release Architecture
proposals.statement: It must distinguish between product-level release artifacts and solution-level release artifacts, because a product may be technically releasable on its own but still not be compatible with a specific solution baseline.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Independent Product Release Compatibility
proposals.statement: It must declare which solution baselines it supports, which interface versions it implements, which data model versions it uses, and which limitations apply.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Independent Product Release Compatibility
proposals.statement: Backward compatibility | Product releases shall not break supported solution baselines unless explicitly approved

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Independent Product Release Compatibility
proposals.statement: Interface versioning | Interfaces shall use defined versioning and deprecation rules

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Independent Product Release Compatibility
proposals.statement: Contract testing | Product releases shall pass contract tests for supported solution baselines

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Independent Product Release Compatibility
proposals.statement: Release declaration | Products shall publish compatibility declarations

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Independent Product Release Compatibility
proposals.statement: Migration support | Breaking changes require migration, rollback, or transition strategy

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Independent Product Release Compatibility
proposals.statement: Every product that participates in a solution must declare compatibility with the applicable solution release baseline.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Independent Product Release Compatibility
proposals.statement: Compatibility must therefore be assessed against a specific solution baseline, not in isolation.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Independent Product Release Compatibility
proposals.statement: A product can be technically ready for release on its own and still be incompatible with a particular solution if interfaces have changed, data semantics are misaligned, security assumptions differ, deployment constraints are not met, or required integration evidence is missing.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Independent Product Release Compatibility
proposals.statement: The Product Architect is responsible for providing the product-level compatibility declaration and supporting evidence.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Independent Product Release Compatibility
proposals.statement: The Solution Architect is responsible for assessing whether the participating products together form a coherent, integrated and releasable solution.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Independent Product Release Compatibility
proposals.statement: The compatibility declaration should be updated whenever the product release, solution baseline, interface contract, data contract, security baseline, deployment topology or integration evidence changes.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integration and Verification Strategy
proposals.statement: Solution-level verification must demonstrate that interfaces, data flows, security assumptions, runtime dependencies, deployment configuration, performance behavior, resilience and release compatibility work together as one coherent solution.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integration and Verification Strategy
proposals.statement: The Solution Architect must define which architecture assumptions require verification, which products are involved, which environments are needed, which evidence is acceptable, and how findings are converted into follow-up actions, technical debt, architecture runway or release blockers.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integration and Verification Strategy
proposals.statement: Verification area | Verification intent | Required evidence

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integration and Verification Strategy
proposals.statement: The integration and verification strategy should be defined early enough to influence solution planning, PI planning, architecture runway and product backlog priorities.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integration and Verification Strategy
proposals.statement: Verification must not be postponed until release readiness if the required evidence depends on missing environments, unavailable product releases, undefined interfaces or unresolved security assumptions.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integration and Verification Strategy
proposals.statement: Solution-level verification should also distinguish between product evidence and integration evidence.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integration and Verification Strategy
proposals.statement: Product evidence shows that a product satisfies its own architecture and quality requirements.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integration and Verification Strategy
proposals.statement: Both are required for release readiness, but they answer different questions.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integration and Verification Strategy
proposals.statement: Findings from integration and verification activities must be fed back into architecture governance.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integration and Verification Strategy
proposals.statement: Failed contract tests, inconsistent schemas, security gaps, deployment failures, performance deviations or resilience weaknesses should be captured as product follow-up actions, solution technical debt, architecture runway, release-readiness risks or guardrail improvement requests.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Integration and Verification Strategy
proposals.statement: A solution release baseline should not be considered release-ready unless the required integration and verification evidence is available, current, owned and traceable to the relevant solution architecture decisions.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Runway
proposals.statement: It captures cross-product enablers that must be available early enough for participating products to implement compatible interfaces, data flows, security mechanisms, deployment assumptions and verification evidence.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Runway
proposals.statement: It is to identify the structural capabilities, shared decisions, technical foundations and integration mechanisms that are required for the solution to evolve safely.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Runway
proposals.statement: Runway items should therefore be linked to concrete solution capabilities, integration risks, release dependencies or quality-marker gaps.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Runway
proposals.statement: Interface runway | Prepare the shared interface foundations required for cross-product integration. | Shared API standards, topic model, interface versioning rules, compatibility test framework, ICD templates

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Runway
proposals.statement: Security runway | Prepare the solution-level security mechanisms required across product boundaries. | Identity model, crypto assumptions, trust-zone model, audit logging, access-control patterns, security verification approach

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Runway
proposals.statement: Platform runway | Prepare the runtime and deployment foundations required for the solution environment. | Runtime architecture, deployment automation, observability model, configuration approach, environment compatibility checks

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Runway
proposals.statement: Solution architecture runway should be reviewed during solution planning, PI planning, integration planning and release-readiness preparation.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Runway
proposals.statement: Each runway item should have a clear owner, affected products, expected delivery horizon, related quality markers and evidence expectation.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Runway
proposals.statement: If a runway item is required for integration or release but is not planned, it should be treated as a solution architecture risk.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Runway
proposals.statement: Runway items should also be connected to the backlog.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Runway
proposals.statement: The Solution Architect is responsible for ensuring that the runway is visible and sufficient at solution level.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Runway
proposals.statement: Product Architects are responsible for implementing the product-level architecture work required by the runway.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Runway
proposals.statement: The solution architecture runway must remain focused.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Runway
proposals.statement: It should not become a general wish list of future improvements.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Runway
proposals.statement: A valid runway item should explain which future capability, integration milestone, release baseline, quality marker or risk reduction it enables.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Runway
proposals.statement: Where the benefit is unclear, the item should either be refined, linked to a concrete dependency, or moved to technical debt or the improvement backlog.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Runway
proposals.statement: A solution release baseline should not be considered robust if critical runway items remain unresolved.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Runway
proposals.statement: Therefore, runway status should be visible in solution architecture reviews and release-readiness assessments.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Risk and Technical Debt Governance
proposals.statement: Solution-level debt shall be tracked separately from product-level technical debt because it affects the relationships between products, not only the internal architecture of one product.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Risk and Technical Debt Governance
proposals.statement: Solution debt should be reviewed during solution planning, PI planning, integration planning, release readiness and Inspect & Adapt.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Risk and Technical Debt Governance
proposals.statement: Every solution debt item should identify the affected products, affected solution baseline, architecture impact, risk level, accountable owner, mitigation action, due date and review point.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Risk and Technical Debt Governance
proposals.statement: Solution debt should also be connected to the appropriate improvement mechanism.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Risk and Technical Debt Governance
proposals.statement: Some items belong in the solution architecture runway because they must be resolved before future integration or release work can proceed.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Risk and Technical Debt Governance
proposals.statement: Others may require a product backlog action, guardrail clarification, platform improvement, security exception or portfolio-level funding decision.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Risk and Technical Debt Governance
proposals.statement: The Solution Architect is responsible for making solution-level debt visible and for ensuring that it is reviewed at the right planning and governance points.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Risk and Technical Debt Governance
proposals.statement: Product Architects are responsible for resolving the product-level actions required to reduce the solution debt.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Risk and Technical Debt Governance
proposals.statement: Repeated or long-lived solution debt should trigger architecture review.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Level Quality Markers
proposals.statement: They should be used during solution architecture reviews, PI planning, integration reviews, system or solution demos, Inspect & Adapt, and release readiness reviews.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Level Quality Markers
proposals.statement: A marker should only be considered mature when it is supported by concrete evidence, such as interface contracts, data contracts, baseline records, compatibility declarations, integration test results, security reviews, deployment evidence, risk records or technical debt items.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Level Quality Markers
proposals.statement: S10 Architecture runway | Are required enablers planned before feature delivery depends on them?

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Quality Marker Catalogue
proposals.statement: They should be used during solution architecture reviews, PI planning, integration planning, system or solution demos, release readiness reviews and Inspect & Adapt.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Quality Marker Catalogue
proposals.statement: A marker should only be considered mature when the required evidence is available, owned, versioned, aligned with applicable enterprise guardrails, and usable by the participating Product Architects.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Quality Marker Catalogue
proposals.statement: ID | Marker | Review question | Required solution evidence

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Quality Marker Catalogue
proposals.statement: The solution markers should be scored using the common maturity scale defined in the SDD Architecture Governance Framework.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Quality Marker Catalogue
proposals.statement: Solution Architecture reviews should therefore distinguish between three questions.

proposals.title: SDD Solution Architecture Guidelines / Solution Architecture Quality Marker Catalogue
proposals.statement: Where a solution marker scores low, the resulting action should be captured as solution architecture runway, solution technical debt, an integration-risk item, a product-level follow-up, a guardrail clarification request, or a release-readiness improvement action.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Purpose
proposals.statement: Solution reviews should be practical and decision-oriented.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Purpose
proposals.statement: They should confirm whether the solution architecture is clear, whether the required product evidence exists, whether ownership is assigned across products, whether release compatibility is understood, and whether follow-up action is required.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Purpose
proposals.statement: A useful solution review should result in one or more of the following outcomes: approval, conditional approval, update to the solution baseline, product-level follow-up action, architecture runway item, integration-risk item, technical debt item, exception request, release-readiness blocker or escalation to Enterprise Architecture.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Purpose
proposals.statement: The outcome of a review should be one of the following:

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Purpose
proposals.statement: Accepted with actions | Architecture is acceptable but improvement actions are required

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Purpose
proposals.statement: Conditionally accepted | A risk or gap must be resolved before a defined milestone

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Purpose
proposals.statement: Escalated | Decision requires higher-level architecture or portfolio involvement

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Review Principles
proposals.statement: Solution reviews shall be held early enough to influence product backlogs, PI planning, architecture runway, integration planning and release readiness.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Review Principles
proposals.statement: Claims of interoperability should be supported by interface contracts and contract tests.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Review Principles
proposals.statement: Claims of data consistency should be supported by data contracts, schemas and semantic mapping evidence.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Review Principles
proposals.statement: Claims of security should be supported by threat models, trust-zone models and verification evidence.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Review Principles
proposals.statement: Claims of release compatibility should be supported by a solution release baseline, product compatibility declarations and integration evidence.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Review Principles
proposals.statement: Solution reviews must also check whether product-level changes affect solution compatibility.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Review Principles
proposals.statement: A product-level ADR may require solution-level review if it changes an externally visible interface, data model, security assumption, runtime dependency, deployment assumption, compatibility declaration or solution baseline.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Review Principles
proposals.statement: The following principles should guide solution architecture reviews:

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Review Principles
proposals.statement: Evidence over presentation | Claims must be proven through documents, tests, demos, measurements, or operational evidence

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Review Principles
proposals.statement: Lightweight but mandatory | Reviews should be efficient, but critical architecture markers cannot be skipped

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Review Principles
proposals.statement: Cross-level alignment | Enterprise, Solution, and Product implications must be visible

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Review Principles
proposals.statement: Early review | Critical architecture issues should be reviewed before implementation becomes expensive

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Review Principles
proposals.statement: Continuous feedback | System demos, Inspect & Adapt, and operational findings must update architecture

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Architecture Review Checklist Reference
proposals.statement: Security, Data and Platform Architects should be involved where the solution review affects trust boundaries, semantic alignment, runtime environments, DevSecOps or deployment architecture.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Architecture Review Checklist Reference
proposals.statement: The review should apply the mandatory BAPO alignment markers in addition to the solution quality markers.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Architecture Review Checklist Reference
proposals.statement: The business capability must be clear, the solution architecture response must be defined, the required integration and release mechanisms must be executable, and ownership must be assigned across the participating products.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Architecture Review Checklist Reference
proposals.statement: A solution should not be considered architecture-ready if product participation, capability allocation, interfaces, data flows, security boundaries, deployment assumptions or integration evidence are still unclear.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Architecture Review Checklist Reference
proposals.statement: A solution should not be considered release-ready unless the required product compatibility declarations, solution baseline, integration evidence, security evidence and release risks are current, owned and reviewable.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Release Readiness
proposals.statement: A solution release shall not be considered ready if participating products are not compatible with the solution baseline, if integration evidence is missing, if security or deployment evidence is incomplete, or if unresolved solution-level risks are not owned and accepted.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Demo and Integration Feedback
proposals.statement: The Solution Architect shall ensure that architecture-relevant findings are converted into owned follow-up actions.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Demo and Integration Feedback
proposals.statement: If the same issue appears repeatedly across products or releases, it should not be treated only as a local defect.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Architecture Exception Handling
proposals.statement: Solution-level exceptions are required when a solution cannot fully comply with an enterprise guardrail, solution baseline, cross-product interface rule, data contract expectation, security boundary, deployment assumption, runtime constraint or release compatibility rule.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Architecture Exception Handling
proposals.statement: The Solution Architect is responsible for identifying whether the deviation affects product participation, capability allocation, cross-product interfaces, data flows, solution security, integrated deployment, integration evidence or release compatibility.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Architecture Exception Handling
proposals.statement: Approved solution exceptions shall be linked to the affected solution baseline, product compatibility matrix, solution risk register, technical debt register or release-readiness record.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Architecture Exception Handling
proposals.statement: Repeated solution exceptions shall be escalated to Enterprise Architecture if they indicate an unclear or outdated enterprise guardrail.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Architecture Exception Handling
proposals.statement: Solution exceptions should remain visible until they are closed, expired or renewed.

proposals.title: Solution Architecture Review and Feedback Process / Solution Architecture Exception Handling
proposals.statement: Repeated solution exceptions should be reviewed as architecture feedback and may indicate an unclear enterprise guardrail, incomplete solution baseline, insufficient product compatibility evidence or missing architecture runway.
